title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Analysis situs (deuxième mouture), June 1986. Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial 'tame topology' of figures. The notation is reconstructed from this page and its neighbours, so the meanings are inferred.
- 𝓕 is a class of figures, partially ordered by ≤ (sub-figure).
- F' ≪ F is a strong or 'interior' sub-figure relation; on p.81 x ≪ X is glossed as x ∈ omb(X)°.
- F'_G is the trace of F' on G. On this page omb F'_G = omb F' ∩ omb G.
- 𝓛 is a class of atomic figures (strata/points). Next page: for x' ∈ 𝓛, any sub-figure is x' or ∅.
- 𝓜 is a class of special 'cell-like' figures.
- omb(F) ('ombre') is the set of atoms making up F, and omb(F)° is its interior part.
- G ‖ F means G and F are dissociated (disjoint/separated); the barred symbol means 'not dissociated'.

Goal (Proposition, p.81): let F' ≪ F, and suppose some non-empty G is dissociated from F' but not from F. Then such a G can be chosen with G ≪ F. In words: if F' fails to 'see' some figure that F sees, the failure is witnessed by an interior piece of F.

Reduction (p.81 to p.82). Using Ax 9, non-dissociation G vs F is detected on atoms. One gets:
- atoms y ∈ omb G and x ∈ omb F with x not ‖ y and y ‖ F';
- a cell X ∈ 𝓜, X ≤ F, with x ≪ X, so that F'_X ≪ X.
The 'initial situation' is thus replaced by a local one: a cell X, its interior sub-figure F'_X, an atom x in the interior of X, and an atom y meeting x but dissociated from F'.

Strategy on p.82: suppose one finds z ∈ omb(X) with z ‖ F'_X. Then z ≪ X ≤ F gives z ≪ F. If moreover z ‖ F', one takes G = z.

The passage from z ‖ F'_X to z ‖ F' is isolated as a Lemma:
- Hypotheses: F' ≪ F, G ≤ F, F'_G ≪ G, H ≤ G.
- Conclusion: if H ‖ F'_G, then H ‖ F'.
- It is to be applied with G = X, H = z.

Proof of the Lemma:
- It suffices to show that for every atom x' ∈ omb F' and every y ∈ omb H we have x' ‖ y.
- Case x' ∈ omb F'_G = omb F' ∩ omb G: this holds by hypothesis.
- Case x' ∈ omb F' \ omb G (finished on p.83): the trace x'_G is x' or ∅ since x' is an atom. It must be ∅, so x' lies outside G while y lies in G. They are therefore distinct strata of the ambient stratification, hence dissociated by axiom 'At 12'.

What remains is the existence of z ∈ omb X dissociated from F'_X but not from X. Grothendieck does not prove this; on p.83 he adopts it as a new axiom At 13, an 'existence of many elements' / completeness axiom. He derives a corollary: F' ≪ F is 'dissociation-equivalent' to F iff no atom of the ambient is dissociated from F'.

In modern terms: a separation/density axiom for a combinatorial stratified-space formalism. Every atom (stratum) disjoint from an interior sub-complex can be detected inside the interior of a cell. It is the analogue of 'closure of a union of strata is detected stratum-wise'.
errors: Notational slip in the lemma's reduction: Grothendieck writes 'x' ∈ omb F', y ∈ omb H ⇒ x ‖ y''; it should read x' ‖ y (the margin 'NB OPS' suggests he noticed a renaming issue).
The lemma's proof is incomplete on this page; the case x' ∉ omb G is finished on p.83 using axiom At 12 (distinct strata are dissociated).
The existence of the required z is not proved; the gap is filled by postulating At 13 on the next page. The Proposition is thus reduced to an axiom, not derived from the earlier axioms.
Hypotheses of the lemma are drawn as a diagram, and the intended relation between H and G (≤ or ≪) is ambiguous in the drawing; the proof only uses omb H ⊂ omb G.

ideas.what: Locality lemma: dissociation of H from the trace F'_G (H inside G) implies dissociation from F', because atoms of F' outside G are distinct strata from those of H.
ideas.modern_name: Stratum-wise detection of disjointness in a stratified space / subcomplex intersection lemma
ideas.where_published: Unpublished Analysis situs notes (1986); the tame topology program is only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6

ideas.what: Reduction of a global existence statement (witness G ≪ F) to a local one in a single cell X ∈ 𝓜 via atoms x ≪ X, preparing the existence axiom At 13 ('existence of many elements', 'completeness').
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology / combinatorial stratified-space axioms; density or separation axiom
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's tame topology program (Esquisse 1984); o-minimal axiomatics by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (only programmatic); the axioms themselves are unpublished

ideas.what: Using a primitive binary 'dissociation' relation ‖ on figures, with atoms 𝓛 and 'ombre' (set of strata), as the basic topological datum rather than open sets.
ideas.modern_name: Contact/connection-relation (mereotopology) style axiomatics of space; Boolean contact algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna; Clarke (1981); Region Connection Calculus (Randell–Cui–Cohn 1992); Düntsch–Vakarelov

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of figures, based on a dissociation relation ‖, atoms and interior relations ≪, closely parallels contact-algebra/mereotopology axiomatizations of space. His At 13-type 'existence of many elements' axiom resembles extensionality/density axioms there. This link does not seem to be noted in the literature on either side.
missed.quote: Pour que l'on ait H ‖ F', il (suffit) que H ‖ F'_G.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give an independent, stratification-flavoured axiom system for tame/region-based topology, comparable with o-minimal and Boolean contact algebra frameworks.

missed.claim: Instead of proving the Proposition, Grothendieck postulates the needed existence statement as a new axiom (At 13). He flags At 8, At 9, At 13 as 'existence of many elements' axioms whose independence and minimality are left open.
missed.quote: Pour trouver un énoncé minimal qui implique la prop
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Determining a minimal axiom set, and checking it against models (semialgebraic/o-minimal stratified sets), remains an open small project within the unpublished tame topology program.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine lemma about stratum-wise disjointness. Interest comes from its place in Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatization of tame topology via a dissociation relation, which is largely absent from the literature, but this page adds little beyond a technical step.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 probably reads 'On veut remplacer la situation initiale par', not 'définition initiale'.
'x ∈ omb(X)° tel que x ‖ y' should carry the bar: x is NOT dissociated from y (x ‖̄ y).
'trouver z ∈ omb(X) telles que z ‖ F'_X': the struck letter is z (rewritten), not deleted content.
'(dans ce cas, on prendra G = z')' – likely 'G = z'.
In the lemma reduction the image reads 'x' ∈ omb F', y ∈ omb H ⇒ x ‖ y'' (a slip for x' ‖ y); the margin reads 'NB OPS H = x, F' = x''.
Last lines: 'On le sait par hyp. si x' ∈ omb F'_G = omb F' ∩ omb G. Si x' ∈ omb F' \ omb F'_G'.
